prize_parts.citation: for showing how collateral constraints and financial frictions amplify and propagate economic fluctuations

statement.case_for: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) gave macroeconomics a tractable general-equilibrium mechanism. Borrowing limits tied to asset values turn small shocks into large, persistent fluctuations. It is conceptually foundational and has nearly three decades of theoretical, quantitative and policy use, with the 2008 crisis as a strong test of its relevance. The Gertler strand (the accelerator with Bernanke, and later intermediary-based models, including the work with Kiyotaki) is what turned the mechanism into quantitative macro models that central banks use. Crediting the three together captures one connected insight: credit frictions are an endogenous propagation channel in the business cycle. The case does not depend on how many members ranked it first. It depends on the mechanism's originality, its breadth across theory, empirics and policy, and its maturity.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is overlap with the 2022 prize to Bernanke, Diamond and Dybvig on banks and financial crises. Adding Gertler brings the Bernanke-Gertler accelerator lineage into the citation, and the Committee may judge that area already honoured. Direct empirical identification of the amplification magnitude is also weaker than the theory's influence suggests. Gertler's wider body of work sits in the crowded New Keynesian candidate B043, so including him could blur credit across ballot items.

responses.point: Kiyotaki and Moore are the sole authors of the foundational paper, so credit is clean. Adding Gertler and Gilchrist would blur the lines given Bernanke's 2022 prize.
responses.response: I accept that the Kiyotaki-Moore pair is the cleanest attribution and that the 2022 overlap is a real risk for the accelerator strand. I still think Gertler is separable from Bernanke's 2022 recognition. That prize rested on banks, runs and crisis analysis, while Gertler's later work with Kiyotaki and with Karadi built quantitative macro models of financial intermediation. That work connects directly to the collateral-constraint mechanism. I keep him as a third name, but I would regard Kiyotaki and Moore alone as an acceptable fallback if the Committee judges the accelerator lineage too close to 2022.

responses.point: Confine the proposal to the two core authors because the accelerator strand partly overlaps the 2022 prize, and Gertler and Gilchrist are related but distinct.
responses.response: This is a fair qualification, and I agree that Gilchrist is better treated as a contributor outside the core. I disagree only on Gertler. The difference between the two-name and three-name versions is a judgment about whether the citation covers credit cycles alone or the broader finding that financial frictions propagate fluctuations. I find the broader scope more faithful to how the literature actually developed. I also recognise that it exposes the award to the overlap objection that you and Dreber raise.

responses.point: Structural estimation of demand and dynamic industry models (B012) is an outstanding example of useful theory tested on data. The BLP core with Pakes as anchor is a clean three-person attribution with no timing obstacle.
responses.response: I did not rank B012 in my opening, and your argument and those of Andersson and Hjalmarsson move me. The methodological reach is broad (merger review, trade, health, environment), the record is three decades long, and the BLP attribution is more compact than in most candidates. My remaining hesitation is the exclusion of Bresnahan and others and the seven credited names. That hesitation does not justify leaving B012 out of my alternatives, so I now name it as one. I still place B002 first because I find the mechanism's conceptual originality and effect on macroeconomic modelling and policy practice greater.

responses.point: Heterogeneous-firm trade (B025) is a foundational change with more than two decades of confirmation, and Melitz is the central author while Redding is a second-generation extender.
responses.response: I agree with the attribution reasoning, which matches my own opening ranking of B025 second with Melitz and Helpman. The main qualification is the overlap with Krugman's 2008 prize and the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum from the credited names, which makes the set incomplete. For these reasons I keep B025 as my first alternative rather than the preferred part. The incompleteness of the credited set is a scientific reason for caution, not only a presentational one.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee treats the accelerator lineage as already covered by the 2022 prize, which decides between the two-name and three-name versions.
Whether Gertler's inclusion is better placed in this prize or reserved for the New Keynesian candidate B043.
How much weight to give the weaker empirical identification of the amplification channel relative to the theory's influence.
For alternatives B025 and B012, whether credited names omitted from the ballot (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum; Bresnahan) should change the laureate set.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent for the preferred candidates (Kiyotaki, Moore, Gertler) from the supplied profile. My profile shows frequent co-authorship with committee colleagues Krusell, Boppart and Friberg, and I work in the adjacent field of macroeconomics, but none of them is a candidate on this configuration. I also have topical affinity with political economy (B050) and social mobility (B015), which are not part of my preferred configuration.
